sections.title: The Restoration of Peter
observations: After the resurrection, Jesus appears to His disciples by the Sea of Tiberias. This event emphasizes the personal relationship Jesus has with His followers, particularly Peter, who had denied Him three times.

Peter's decision to go fishing reflects a return to his old life, possibly out of confusion or guilt after his denial of Christ. However, Jesus meets him in this familiar setting, showing that He is still present in Peter's life.
The miraculous catch of fish serves as a reminder of Jesus' earlier call to Peter and the other disciples, highlighting His authority and the abundance He provides.

sections.title: The Conversation with Peter
observations: Jesus' three questions to Peter, 'Do you love me?' serve to restore Peter after his three denials. This repetition emphasizes the importance of love and commitment in the relationship between Jesus and His followers.
Jesus commands Peter to 'feed my sheep,' indicating that love for Christ is demonstrated through service to others. This sets the foundation for Peter's future role as a leader in the early church.
The conversation also foreshadows the challenges Peter will face, including martyrdom, which underscores the cost of discipleship.

sections.title: The Future of John
observations: Peter's curiosity about John's future leads to a misunderstanding about Jesus' intentions. Jesus' response highlights the importance of focusing on one's own calling rather than comparing oneself to others.
This section teaches that each disciple has a unique path and purpose in God's plan, and it encourages believers to remain faithful to their own calling without distraction.

importantVerses.commentary: Jesus asks Peter three times if he loves Him, emphasizing the importance of love in the relationship between Christ and His followers.
Jesus commands Peter to 'feed my sheep,' highlighting the responsibility of leaders in the church to care for the flock.
Jesus' response to Peter about John teaches the importance of focusing on one's own calling rather than comparing oneself to others.

questions: What does Peter's restoration teach us about forgiveness and grace?
How can we apply Jesus' command to 'feed my sheep' in our own lives?
What does this chapter reveal about the nature of discipleship and following Christ?
